item.title: Two quantum spin liquid states coexisting in the kagome antiferromagnet herbertsmithite
item.description: arXiv:2610.24065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Herbertsmithite (ZnCu$_3$(OH)$_6$Cl$_2$) is one of the most extensively studied quantum spin liquid (QSL) candidates, yet the precise nature of its ground state remains unresolved. Here, we compare the results of high-resolution inelastic neutron scattering on single crystals of herbertsmithite (Zn$_\mathrm{x}$Cu$_\mathrm{4-x}$(OD)$_6$Cl$_2$, $x\simeq 0.85$) with large-scale density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and dynamical DMRG simulations to benchmark the spin Hamiltonian and uncover fundamental properties of the ground state. The measured spin correlations determine an energy density for the Heisenberg model that closely matches simulations, an essential verification of the Hamiltonian. In parallel, DMRG simulations reveal two nearly degenerate QSL states. Both preserve translational symmetry, but one retains the lattice point-group symmetries whereas the other develops anisotropic spin correlations that break point-group symmetry. These two QSLs have distinct spin structure factors, and, remarkably, close agreement with the neutron spectra is achieved with an admixture of the two states. Our results establish a quantitative correspondence between neutron scattering and simulations, and suggest that herbertsmithite realizes a regime in which two proximate gapped QSL states coexist.
item.dc:creator: Arthur C. Campello, Shengtao Jiang, Wei He, Jiajia Wen, Daniel M. Pajerowski, Steven A. Kivelson, Hong-Chen Jiang, Young S. Lee

item.title: Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics
item.description: arXiv:2610.24071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kagome lattice materials host a remarkably rich landscape of novel quantum phenomena, all arising from the intrinsic interplay of topology, correlation, and frustration. While previous studies have been mostly limited to bulk three-dimensional (3D) kagome crystals, the realization of a true two-dimensional (2D) kagome system has remained a long-standing goal, to unlock fundamentally new physics and engineering pathways inaccessible in 3D systems. In this work, we establish the first ideal 2D monolayer kagome lattices by leveraging a novel and versatile van der Waals (vdW) kagome family, A2T3X4 (A = K, Rb, Cs; T = Ni, Pd, Pt; X = S, Se). Our nano-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) directly characterizes the electronic structure of A2T3X4 down to the monolayer limit, notably revealing an isolated kagome-derived flat band just below the Fermi level. Via gate-engineering of 2D A2T3X4, the kagome flat band can be further tuned to the Fermi level, allowing direct access to the partially filled flat band physics and establishing a qualitatively new 2D flat band platform. Compared to existing moire-based artificial flat band systems, this vdW kagome-based intrinsic flat band system realizes more than 220 times higher flat band electron density, opening an entirely new density and energy regime for exploring 2D flat band physics. Harnessing this high-electron-density flat band in 2D vdW kagome system provides a clear pathway to scale emergent flat band phenomena - such as fractional quantum anomalous Hall states - to far higher temperatures than currently achievable, as long-envisioned in theory and further supported by our many-body calculations.

item.title: Kohler's Rule Holds in the Strange Metallic Hubbard Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.24208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unconventional magnetotransport violating Kohler's rule has been reported in many strongly correlated strange metals, but the exact origin of these violations is yet unknown. To investigate this question, we use determinant quantum Monte Carlo to compute the magnetoresistance of the hole-doped Hubbard-Hofstadter model. Despite $T$-linear resistivity exceeding the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit and the nominal absence of well-defined quasiparticles, we find Kohler's rule unexpectedly holds across a wide range of on-site interaction strengths and hole dopings. In particular, Kohler emerges below a crossover temperature $T^\star\approx t$ identified from the double occupancy and specific heat, coinciding with the onset of local singlet correlations between lattice sites. We thus propose that Kohler scaling in this regime reflects a more general form of many-body quantum coherence. Our results show that strong correlations and strange metallicity do not themselves generically produce anomalous magnetoresistance.
item.dc:creator: Rebekah M. Jin, Emily Z. Zhang, Jixun K. Ding, Brian Moritz, Thomas P. Devereaux

item.title: Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A$_2$T$_3$X$_4$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moir\'e materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the recently synthesized van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Exact diagonalization of models derived from density functional theory reveals ferromagnetism over broad filling ranges, supporting diverse fractional Chern insulators, anomalous composite Fermi liquids, and charge-ordered phases. In particular, in $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{Pd}_3\mathrm{S}_4$, the fractional Chern insulator exhibits a many-body gap of approximately 26 meV in the largest system accessible with band mixing allowing at most one interband electron-hole excitation. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced energy scales and control over topological order.
item.dc:creator: Soomin Oh, Jiyong Han, Jinhyeok Choi, Donghae Seo, Mingu Kang, Gil Young Cho

item.title: Microwave probing of magnetic phases in a dipolar-exchange magnet LiGdF$_4$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the results of low-temperature magnetic resonance measurements performed on a single-crystal sample of a weakly anisotropic dipolar-exchange antiferromagnet LiGdF$_4$. The transformation of a resonance spectrum due to the formation of the ordered phase is observed at temperatures below $T_N=0.19(1)$ K. A sequence of field-induced phase transitions is detected for the external magnetic field applied along the fourfold axis of the crystal. A well-resolved magnetic resonance spectrum is observed in one of the low-field magnetic phases as well as above the saturation field. Competing exchange and dipolar interactions, as a special type of magnetic frustration, are suggested to account for the delayed ordering and complex magnetic phase diagram of the system.
item.dc:creator: S. S. Sosin, A. I. Smirnov, T. A. Soldatov, V. S. Edelman, O. A. Morozov, S. L. Korableva, I. V. Romanova

item.title: Interaction-driven competing instabilities in two-dimensional checkerboard quadratic band crossing semimetals
item.description: arXiv:2610.25046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional quadratic band crossing point (QBCP) semimetals serve as a fertile platform for interaction-driven quantum criticality, nevertheless, the role of the complete fermion-fermion interactions remains largely unexplored. To address this, we systematically investigate the low-energy physics of a spin-1/2 checkerboard-lattice QBCP semimetal by considering all 16 marginally short-range fermion-fermion interactions. Using the momentum-shell renormalization group, we derive the coupled flow equations, which reveal that the low-energy physics is governed by a series of fixed points. Depending on the initial conditions, the system may exhibit a single stable fixed point, several discrete fixed points, or three continuous groups of fixed points parameterized by a few variables. By introducing source terms and evaluating susceptibilities, we identify the dominant and subdominant instabilities. The leading phases include nematic spin-nematic (NSN), quantum anomalous Hall (QAH), chiral superconducting ($\mathrm{SC}_1$), and quantum spin Hall (QSH) orders. Moreover, several features distinguish our findings from previous simplified models. Off-diagonal interactions generate terms that promote orders absent in such models, the continuous groups allow systematic tuning of the leading instability, and trajectory-dependent instabilities emerge where the full RG flow, rather than the fixed point alone, determines the dominant state. These results offer a comprehensive theoretical understanding of low-energy quantum critical behaviors and phase instabilities in two-dimensional QBCP semimetals and related electron systems.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Hao Wen, Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

item.title: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions and deconfined criticality in SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$ is the leading candidate for deconfined criticality, yet theories of its critical regime omit the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions, which gap the kagome Dirac spin liquid. Adding them to the SU(2) gauge theory, we show that time reversal and a spin-orbit-locked glide forbid any gauge-singlet spinon mass to all orders. In-plane DM only twists the spinons, reconstructing the nodes below $0.03$-$0.17$ K, while out-of-plane DM is irrelevant and SO(5) anisotropy arises only at second order. The material thus remains a platform for deconfined criticality, which NMR can test, since a $[100]$ field induces a N\'eel moment and a $[001]$ field does not.
item.dc:creator: Yasir Iqbal

item.title: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions in the SU(2) gauge theory of the Shastry-Sutherland Dirac spin liquids
item.description: arXiv:2610.25082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the fermion bilinears of the SU(2) gauge theory of the Shastry-Sutherland Dirac spin liquids under the spin-orbit-locked space group and treat the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions of SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$ at leading order in $1/N$ and at one loop. At linear order DM can neither gap the spinons nor destabilize the SO(5) point above a scale $T^*$. Symmetry forbids every local gauge-singlet fermion mass at any order. Among the singlet bilinears, the in-plane couplings induce only a conserved spin current of dimension exactly 2, which sets $T^*=4\lambda\simeq0.03$-$0.17$ K, and the out-of-plane coupling only a flavored spin-2 current, irrelevant at a unitary critical point. DM-induced Yukawa couplings start below $2\%$ of the one that bounds the pseudocritical window. In zero field, measured samples order above $1$ K, at or above $T^*$. Below $T^*$, in a two-dimensional sample at the critical pressure, the Dirac cones reconstruct into a chirally protected $d$-wave quadratic band touching whose only gauge-singlet gap channels are the two valence-bond components and the scalar chirality. A one-loop flow, with the gauge field screened by the band touching, ends at $T^{**}\sim(0.03$-$0.1)\lambda$ on a ray containing valence-bond order for the material's exchange and for most random couplings, and otherwise on a gapped chiral $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquid. The DM bias between the two plaquette patterns is at most of order $10^{-4}$, with a direction not fixed at $O(1/N)$, whereas non-magnetic quenched disorder couples a relevant random field to the plaquette doublet and none to the chirality. A field along $[100]$ induces a $(\pi,\pi)$ N\'eel moment linear in the field; a field along $[001]$ does not. This selection rule also holds in the dimer phase and is testable by $^{11}$B NMR under pressure.
item.dc:creator: Yasir Iqbal

item.title: Large exchange bias from coupled antiferromagnetic order and glassy magnetic freezing in $Co_{0.36}NbS_{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetization measurements on single-crystalline $Co_{0.36}NbS_{2}$ reveal antiferromagnetic order near $T_{N} \simeq 26 K$ and a lower-temperature history-dependent magnetic response consistent with glassy freezing of a subset of magnetic moments. After field cooling, $M(H)$ loops exhibit a sizable exchange-bias shift, reaching $|H_{EB}| \simeq 4.4 kOe$ at $1.8 K$ for a $70 kOe$ field-cooling sweep protocol. The training effect, field-sweep and cooling-field protocol dependence, and disappearance of the bias near a blocking temperature $T_{B} \simeq 12 K$, well below $T_{N}$, support an interpretation in which frozen uncompensated moments are exchange-coupled to an antiferromagnetic matrix. These results suggest that antiferromagnetic-glassy-moment coupling may provide a broader route to exchange bias in off-stoichiometric magnetic $NbS_{2}$ intercalates.

item.title: Frustration-Assisted Electrical Switching in $Co_xTaS_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrical switching in antiferromagnets is commonly described as the action of current-induced torques on a rigid order parameter. In frustrated magnets, however, competing states can create a history-dependent energy landscape in which slow collective dynamics actively participate in electrical reconfiguration. Here, we demonstrate frustration-assisted switching in near-stoichiometric $Co_xTaS_2$, a van der Waals antiferromagnet located at the composition-sensitive boundary between Hall-active and Hall-inactive multi-Q-related magnetic regimes. Although the crystals exhibit no resolved spontaneous Hall response, they retain van Hove singularities near the Fermi level and order antiferromagnetically below $T_N \simeq 31.5 K$. Current pulses write nonvolatile anisotropic resistance states in microstructured devices, with an activation current density nearly an order of magnitude below that reported for the Hall-active lower-intercalation phase. The switching response separates into two temperature-dependent dynamical regimes rather than following a single current threshold. Independent magnetization-aging and post-field-relaxation measurements reveal slow, history-dependent magnetic dynamics, and the relaxation strength closely follows the inverse switching amplitude. These results identify magnetic frustration and glassy dynamics as central ingredients in the electrical reconfiguration of $Co_xTaS_2$, establishing a route to functional switching through a dynamically soft antiferromagnetic landscape.

item.title: Categorical classification of non-Fermi liquids in 2+1 dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.25713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A defining feature of non-Fermi liquids is a lack of the quasiparticle peak on the Fermi surface in the spectral function, which is usually realized by coupling a finite density of fermions with critical collective fluctuations. However, these features of the two- and three-point vertex functions are qualitatively the same across many non-Fermi liquids, which has made it difficult to classify them beyond the definition by negation. We point out that the four-point function in the pairing channel contains rich information that positively differentiates distinct types of non-Fermi liquids. Using the generalized notion of fixed points that captures scale-dependent universal pairing interaction, we provide a non-perturbative classification of 2+1-dimensional non-Fermi liquids. In the large Fermi momentum limit with fixed dimensionless couplings, metals coupled with long-wavelength critical fluctuations are classified into seven superuniversality classes. Each of them exhibits a unique phase diagram in the space of temperature and bare four-fermion coupling. The present work generalizes the earlier perturbative classification to strongly interacting non-Fermi liquids by leveraging kinematic constraints.
item.dc:creator: Shubham Kukreja, Dawson M. Willerton, Sung-Sik Lee

item.title: Ferroelastic domain wall driven glassy dynamics and photoresponse in a SrTiO$_3$ (111) two-dimensional electron gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.25943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The (111) orientation of SrTiO$_3$ (STO)-based heterostructures has emerged as a versatile platform for two-dimensional electron gases (2DEGs), yet the influence of STO's polar ferroelastic domain-wall (DW) network on charge transport remains largely unexplored. Here we study AlO$_x$/STO (111) interfaces hosting 2DEGs of different carrier densities. In the lower-density 2DEG, low-temperature transport exhibits thermal hysteresis, slow resistance relaxation, cooling-rate dependence, and memory effects, signaling glasslike electron dynamics. The relaxation is strongly non-monotonic in temperature, increasing below $\sim$80 K, peaking near 25 K, and vanishing below $\sim$12 K, tracking the established evolution of the ferroelastic DW state of bulk STO rather than any electronic energy scale, which identifies the DW network as its origin. These signatures are absent in a second, more metallic interface with much higher carrier density, demonstrating that the electron-DW coupling can be tuned. We further show that polar DWs govern the photoresponse: the persistent photoconductivity rises sharply below $\sim$80 K, coinciding with the onset of DW polarity. Together, these results establish polar ferroelastic DWs as a carrier-density-tunable electronic degree of freedom in STO (111)-based 2DEGs, opening routes to manipulate 2DEG properties through topological defects.
item.dc:creator: Jyotirmay Maity, Manav Beniwal, Pranab Hazra, Sumit Tomar, Srimanta Middey

item.title: Methods of density functional theory in one dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.26012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Density functional theory is formally justified by an existence proof. As such, the need for computational methods to study the theory is a useful route to understanding the full theory. In this paper, we discuss the numerical strategies to efficiently evaluate computations for Kohn-Sham systems in one dimension and also methods for determining exact properties, including time-dependence. An accompanying library is also available for computing one-dimensional density functional theory and publicly available. The expressions used to implement the density functional in one-dimension are surveyed. An alternative justification for a gradient-based technique is also shown that can be applied to time-dependent evolution of the exact Kohn-Sham potential.
item.dc:creator: Thomas E. Baker, Kasey Chen

item.title: Evidence of valence bond solid and quantum paramagnetism in the $J_1$--$J_2$--$J_3$ Heisenberg model from pseudofermion functional renormalization group
item.description: arXiv:2610.26135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by recent tensor network studies reporting a quantum spin liquid (QSL) within the quantum paramagnetic (QP) regime, we investigate numerically the zero-temperature phase diagram of the $J_1$--$J_2$--$J_3$ Heisenberg model on the square lattice using the pseudofermion functional renormalization group (pf-fRG). Thanks to improved frequency resolution and larger lattice truncations, we are able to explore a significantly larger parameter space than previous pf-fRG work to map out the phase boundary of an extended QP region. We further resolve possible bond order within the QP regime by measuring the dimer response to small deformations in $J_1$, i.e. bond anisotropy that breaks the point-group symmetry of the Hamiltonian. The functional renormalization group flow of the dimer susceptibility suggests that the QP window splits into two: a region where it grows continuously down to the lowest energy scale to signal valence bond solid (VBS) order, and another region where it reaches a peak at a finite scale and is subsequently suppressed to indicate a QSL.
item.dc:creator: G\"un G\"unal, Erhai Zhao, Ahmet Kele\c{s}

item.title: High-order resonances and emergent coherent dynamics in interacting Stark chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.26328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A linear potential gradient can strongly suppress quantum dynamics, while interactions can activate resonant many-body processes whose higher-order structure remains largely unexplored. Here we uncover a systematic hierarchy of high-order interaction--tilt resonances in an interacting Stark chain, where the resonance order counts the minimal number of elementary exchange steps involved. These resonances manifest as long-lived coherent oscillations with order-dependent timescales. By isolating individual resonant channels and developing a microscopic effective description, we connect these dynamical timescales to the underlying many-body exchange processes and reveal a pronounced dependence on the initial-state structure. Our results provide crucial insights into high-order many-body resonances and show how commensurate interaction-to-tilt ratios generate a hierarchy of parametrically slow coherent many-body dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Jiahe Chang, Hongzheng Zhao

item.title: Variational Block Correlated Coupled Cluster Monte Carlo
item.description: arXiv:2610.26646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the recent success of quantum neural states, we present a variational implementation of the coupled cluster method suitable for quantum Monte Carlo simulations. We introduce a Young tableaux representation of the wave-function coefficients and their derivatives that substantially reduces the computational complexity of the variational optimization. While the algorithm is generic, we illustrate its implementation with an application to the Heisenberg model in one and two dimensions, using the block correlated coupled cluster ansatz (BCCC) with doubles and triples. Convergence is greatly improved by means of importance sampling based on a fictitious temperature. The resulting approach achieves competitive accuracy while providing a scalable framework for variational coupled-cluster calculations.
item.dc:creator: Hunter Brodie, Alexander Shilcusky, Adrian E. Feiguin

item.title: Kondo Lattice model for field induced triplet pairing in CeRh$_2$As$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.26858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin triplet superconductors are of interest because of their topological properties, and their robustness to high magnetic fields. CeRh$_2$As$_2$ is a unique heavy fermion superconductor with both even-parity and candidate odd-parity superconducting phases with a special feature enabling a field induced phase transition between the two. The field induced transition which switches the parity of the Cooper pairs is enabled by a staggered antisymmetric spin orbit coupling (ASOC) interaction. However, the heavy fermion origins of the superconductivity in CeRh$_2$As$_2$ and the origin of the antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling are currently unexplored. Here, we develop a Kondo lattice model for CeRh$_2$As$_2$ and demonstrate how local hybridization between Cerium $d$- and $f$-orbitals, driven by the locally broken inversion symmetry, at the Cerium sites generates the ASOC. The resulting Kondo lattice model leads to nearly degenerate even and odd parity superconducting states that display a field induced parity transition between an even-parity state and an odd-parity pseudospin triplet state. We discuss the wider implications of our results extended to other heavy fermion systems like CeSiI.
item.dc:creator: Indra Gankhuyag, Piers Coleman

item.title: On Higher-Form Fracton Hydrodynamics with Momentum Conservation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Momentum conservation is common in fluids, yet it may be incompatible with the hydrodynamics of theories with exotic conservation laws (such as fracton hydrodynamics) unless symmetries are spontaneously broken. Using the Martin-Siggia-Rose (MSR) effective field theory formalism, we develop a representation-theoretic framework for the hydrodynamics of translationally invariant systems with exotic conservation laws without spontaneous symmetry breaking. Under mild assumptions on the form of hydrodynamics, we show that such theories must satisfy two representation theoretic consistency conditions and a generalized Gauss's law constraint. Higher-form symmetries satisfy these conditions and we derive their ideal hydrodynamics; in three dimensions, the one-form case produces ideal non-relativistic magnetohydrodynamics. Finally, we prove that no other theories are compatible with momentum conservation in SO(3) nor SO($d$), for sufficiently large odd $d$.
item.dc:creator: Ben Bobell, Rahul Nandkishore, Andrew Lucas

item.title: Quantum-interference correction to conductivity in disordered electronic bands with non-uniform quantum geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.22500v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weak localization in two-dimensional disordered electron systems originates from constructive interference between time-reversed scattering paths, giving rise to a logarithmically divergent quantum-interference correction to the dc conductivity. This behavior is generally suppressed when time-reversal symmetry (TRS) is broken. In this study, using a band-projected framework motivated by spin- and valley-polarized rhombohedral $N$-layer graphene (RNG), we show that nonuniform quantum geometry can qualitatively modify quantum-interference corrections to dc transport. In particular, continuously tuning the quantum geometry can change the sign of the conductivity correction, corresponding to a crossover between localization and antilocalization tendencies. Remarkably, at special values of the parameter controlling the quantum geometry, weak-localization (WL) or weak-antilocalization (WAL) can re-emerge despite broken microscopic TRS. At these special points, the orbital structure of the Bloch states gives rise to an emergent antiunitary symmetry that protects a gapless Cooperon mode and restores the logarithmically divergent quantum-interference correction characteristic of WL or WAL. Our results establish nonuniform quantum geometry as a mechanism for controlling quantum interference and electron localization in multiorbital electronic systems.
item.dc:creator: Yip Chun Wong, Asimpunya Mitra, Yong Baek Kim

item.title: Universal electrical resistivity in iron-based high-temperature superconductors
item.description: arXiv:2610.23865v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity $\rho(T)$ in cuprate, iron-based, and nickelate superconductors represents one of unresolved problems in modern solid-state physics, because of the high absolute value of $\rho(T)$, which, in many cases, exceeds the Ioffe-Rigel criterion, and a large difference in the $\rho(T)$ shape for samples with different doping. Here I show that the nearest neighbors parallel resistivity model (arXiv: 2607.23484) can well describe the in-plane resistivity $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in iron-based superconductors (IBS) of type 11, 111, 122, 1111, 1144 and 42214 in which the spin density wave phase or nematic order is suppressed by doping. The model is based on the postulate that $\rho_{ab}(T)$ is a sum of two parallel conduction channels, where one channel is described by the Bloch-Gr\"uneisen equation and the other by the Arrhenius hopping equation. Consequently, the variety of $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in the IBS is explained as a variation of the Debye temperature $\Theta_D$ and the hopping activation energy $E_a$. The derived Debye temperatures were used to estimate the electron-phonon coupling constant $\lambda_{e-ph}$in the studied IBS.
item.dc:creator: E. F. Talantsev

item.title: CME-SpectrumBench: Can LLMs Analyze Condensed Matter Spectral Data?
item.description: arXiv:2610.24304v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are presently well assessed by expert-level mathematics and physics benchmarks which focus on theoretical, symbolic reasoning. However, we lack experimental benchmarks that evaluate data analysis in frontier research problems, a capability that future domain-specific foundation models must have. To this end, we present CME-SpectrumBench, an expert-designed benchmark consisting of 190 questions that measures how reliably frontier LLMs analyze research-level spectral scientific data in condensed matter experiments (CME). Using simulated CME spectral data, we prompt models to identify structures from 2D intensity arrays in the face of noise and limited instrumental resolution, a test of dense context reasoning. Models are scored by how accurately their numerical answers approach the ground truth. Under direct query, scores generally pale in comparison to handwritten code due to clear failure modes: models can find simple features but struggle to trace patterns or compute derived quantities, and performance typically degrades with increased data resolution and noise/convolution levels. LLM performance becomes comparable to handwritten code by allowing tool use (access to a Python interpreter) with/without ReAct prompting, in effect mapping questions onto agentic code generation problems. Our findings show that frontier models can serve as research assistants by interfacing with data through code, but still face difficulties processing information directly from large datasets - a key barrier future foundation models must overcome. The code and data are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/jingene/CMESpectrumBench.
item.dc:creator: Jin Gene Wong, Anjney Midha, Joseph Mathew Tennyson, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica, Zhi-Xun Shen

item.title: Certifying Nonlocal Spin Quantum Entanglement from Local Tunneling Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2610.24440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum entanglement is intrinsically nonlocal, whereas tunneling spectroscopy measures one site at a time. We show that this apparent mismatch can be overcome: local tunneling spectra can certify spin entanglement without coherent control or absolute intensity calibration. An exact spin sum rule turns the high-bias conductance into an internal normalization, allowing the inelastic spin-flip weight to place a lower bound on the local quantum Fisher information. Total-spin conservation then fixes the otherwise inaccessible intersite fluctuation, converting two local spectra into a bound on a collective entanglement witness. We incorporate coupling to the substrate through a spectroscopic bound on spin leakage, while a hierarchy of thresholds distinguishes entanglement between the spins from entanglement with their environment. Including instrumental broadening and noise, the resulting certificate holds at a stated confidence level. These results establish a route for extracting nonlocal quantum information from equilibrium local spectroscopy.
item.dc:creator: Payman Kazemikhah, Ruolun Zhang, Xiangyu Luo, Byunghoon Kim, Yu-Peng Zhu, Md. Shafayat Hossain, M. Zahid Hasan

item.title: Accurate Atomic Correlation Energies and Virial Trends for Correlation-Consistent Effective Core Potentials III: Quantitative Separation of Fixed-Node Biases and Localization Errors in Cs-Rn
item.description: arXiv:2610.24450v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Atomic benchmarks for sixth-period elements (Cs-Rn) are established to sub-millihartree precision under correlation-consistent effective core potentials (ccECPs) using coupled-cluster [up to CCSDT(Q)] and full configuration interaction methods. These references systematically characterize electron correlation, potential-to-kinetic energy partitioning, and combined fixed-node and locality biases ($\eta$) in fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo (FNDMC). The valence kinetic-to-total energy ratio ($\xi$) departs from the non-relativistic all-electron Coulombic virial limit ($\xi=100\%$), remaining confined between 25.8$\%$ and 37.6$\%$. The Un-pseudizing of semi-core shells decreases $\xi$ as the attractive potential energy deepens faster than the accompanying kinetic energy escalates. Periodic trends in $\xi$ reveal a $5d$ plateau near 34$\%$, with a lanthanide-contraction-driven maximum in Hf, followed by a sharp decline across the $6p$ block. In FNDMC, $\eta$ escalates rapidly at the onset of group-1/2 and toward the $6p$ closed-shell limit, peaking at 5.42$\%$ in Rn. Although fixed-node errors dominate $\eta$ in most sixth-period elements, a locality error inversion occurs in Bi, with Pb exhibiting comparable error magnitudes. Furthermore, core-valence partitioning alters trial wavefunction nodal topology: in Tl, three-dimensional nodal cross-sections reveal isolated toroidal domains that confine walkers. This work completes the periodic-table-wide ccECP database from H to Rn, revealing how pseudopotential choices govern energy partitioning, nodal topology, and the balance between fixed-node and localization errors.
item.dc:creator: Omar Madany, Lubos Mitas

item.title: Turning Number and the Geometry of Disorder-Induced Topology
item.description: arXiv:2610.24637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps derived from the zero-frequency single-particle Green's function provides a route to a refined topological characterization of quantum systems beyond the noninteracting clean limit. The central idea is to complement standard topological invariants by invariants that characterize the geometry of the map itself. As a paradigmatic example, we study the one-dimensional chiral Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with disorder, where the topological Hamiltonian defines a planar Bloch loop. In addition to its conventional winding number, this loop possesses an integer turning number that characterizes the winding of its tangent vector. We identify turning-number transitions that occur while the topological Hamiltonian remains finite and spectrally gapped, driven solely by a vanishing tangent vector of the Bloch loop, and obtain an extended phase diagram with additional topological structure beyond the winding-number classification. Asymptotic analysis predicts the emergence and disorder dependence of the corresponding transition regime, in agreement with the numerical results. Our findings establish the geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps as an additional source of topological structure beyond conventional classifications.
item.dc:creator: Lars Emmrich, Michael Potthoff

item.title: Vortexable Chern Bands Sit Exactly on the Topological Floor of Flat-Band Superfluid Stiffness
item.description: arXiv:2610.24877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vortexable Chern bands host ideal fractional Chern insulators. Paired with time-reversed partners by orbital-diagonal on-site attraction, they are the least stiff flat-band superconductors at fixed Chern number $C$, filling, and pairing amplitude. For uniform pairing and a nondegenerate paired state, the exact $T=0$ stiffness determinant is the topological floor times $1+(\Torb/2\pi|C|)^2\le1+(\TLVP/2\pi|C|)^2$, where $\Torb$ and $\TLVP$ measure departures from vortexability. Enhancement costs vortexability, and the inequality is strict only if internal components share a site, as in heterostrained bilayers.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Wang, Samuel L. Braunstein

item.title: Random spin-3/2 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains revisited
item.description: arXiv:2610.24994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit the spin-reduction transition in the random spin-$3/2$ antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain using the tensor-network strong-disorder renormalization group (tSDRG). The predicted transition separates two random-singlet (RS) phases: one formed by effective spin-$1/2$ moments at weaker disorder and the other by full spin-$3/2$ moments at stronger disorder. Within the Damle--Huse classification, this transition corresponds to an emergent permutation-symmetric $\mathcal{P}_4$ multicritical point on a $\mathcal{P}_2$ critical line associated with the RS phases. We first derive the critical exponents governing the disorder-averaged bulk and end-to-end correlation functions in the $\mathcal{P}_n$ universality classes within the Damle--Huse framework. Using these theoretical predictions, together with a diagnostic constructed from the mean and variance of the energy-gap distribution, we identify the $\mathcal{P}_4$ transition point and the reentrant behavior of the RS phase.
item.dc:creator: Yen-Tung Lin, Pochung Chen, Yu-Cheng Lin

item.title: Electronic structure, magnetic order and anisotropic magnetoresistance in $\mathbf{Eu_{1-x}Gd_xCd_2P_2}$ (0 $\le$ x $\le$1)
item.description: arXiv:2610.25194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, $\text{EuCd}_2\text{P}_2$ has attracted increased attention for its colossal magnetoresistive (CMR) property, the mechanism of which seems to deviate from that of known canonical CMR compounds such as manganites. Many studies underscore the role of low density of hole carriers caused by Eu vacancies, particularly in stabilizing ferromagnetic (FM) order and modifying electrical transport and magnetoresistive responses in this compound. A magnetic polaron based mechanism rather than double exchange based mechanism is being proposed to explain the CMR effect for this compound. In this work, we explore the effect of elctron doping on the magnetic transition and CMR behaviour via Gd substitution at Eu sites with varying concentration (x) in Eu$_{1-x}$Gd$_{x}$Cd$_2$P$_2$. Our Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Monte Carlo-based calculations reveal an oscillating ground state magnetic order as a function of electron carrier density. The ground state is found to be A-AFM metal for x=0.056, 0.125 and 0.5 while it becomes ferromagnetic metal at x= 0.33, 0.67 and 1. Most importantly, we predict colossal anisotropic magnetoresistance in this compound for x=0.125 and 0.5. The underlying mechanism of anisotropic CMR in this compound looks similar to double exchange like due to the presence of a strong intra-site 4\textit{f}-5\textit{d} ferromagnetic exchange interaction and an itinerant electron in the hybridized conduction states. The oscillating ground state magnetic order and the enhancement of transition temperature (as high as 150K for x=0.67) as a function of electron carrier density offers a new avenue to tune the magnetotransport property in this compound and offers an excellent platform for designing future spintronics devices.
item.dc:creator: Yogendra Singh Negi, Tulika Maitra

item.title: Upper Bound on the Correlation Energy of a Dense Fermi Gas in the Thermodynamic Limit
item.description: arXiv:2610.25262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the random phase approximation provides an upper bound on the correlation energy of a three-dimensional, weakly interacting, Fermi gas in the thermodynamic limit at high density. More precisely, we consider a mean-field scaling regime where the kinetic and interaction Hamiltonian are scaled by $\rho^{-2/3}$ and $\rho^{-1}$, respectively. We use a correlated trial state constructed through a quasi-bosonic Bogoliubov transformation of collective particle--hole excitations associated to patches on the Fermi surface. Key of the proof is to control the position-space localization of the collective excitations. Combined with an iterated Duhamel expansion of the expectation values of (localized) particle number operators we obtain extensive estimates, which justify the reduction to an effective quadratic Hamiltonian and its approximate diagonalization.
item.dc:creator: Niels Benedikter, Sascha Lill, Marcello Porta, Benjamin Schlein

item.title: Tensor network Monte Carlo study of the J1-J2 Ising model on the square lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.25270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The frustrated square-lattice J1-J2 Ising model exhibits rich magnetic phases, yet its phase transitions remain difficult to characterize due to critical slowing down in conventional Monte Carlo and truncation errors inherent to tensor renormalization group methods.We develop a tensor-network Monte Carlo (TNMC) algorithm for this frustrated model, which supports both open and periodic boundary conditions. For periodic lattices, we use a sweeping block-update strategy that updates spin blocks while fixing surrounding spins.To boost efficiency, we couple our sampler with histogram reweighting, and test each technique standalone to validate these independent optimizations.We perform extensive finite-size scaling analyses at g=0.55 and g=1.0, extracting apparent critical temperatures and effective thermal exponents from Binder-cumulant data.Our method offers an efficient, nearly bias-free path for large-scale simulations of J1-J2-type frustrated magnets under periodic boundaries and generalizes readily to other frustrated spin lattices.
item.dc:creator: Wanying Zheng, Tao Chen, Youjin Deng, Wanzhou Zhang

item.title: The Anyon Atlas
item.description: arXiv:2610.25439v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify possible topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions with up to 22 anyons in the bosonic case and up to 26 in the fermionic case, through the modular data of modular and supermodular tensor categories. We construct such data via congruence representations of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ using a numerical optimization algorithm that scales to high rank. We chart the relations between the resulting theories, including anyon condensations and Chern-Simons realizations. We find examples of modular data that do not appear to arise from any Chern-Simons theory by any sequence of condensations of anyons or gaugings of ordinary global symmetries. These examples give qualitatively new topological quantum field theories, which go beyond any notion of gauge theory. For examples in this class with 11 and 12 anyon types, we solve the pentagon and hexagon equations explicitly, showing that these modular data are realized by full unitary topological quantum field theories. We also introduce https://www.AnyonAtlas.org, an online resource for exploring the data.
item.dc:creator: Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham

item.title: Topological Quantum Gates on FCIs with Bounded Quantum Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.25472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two-band 2D fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) have recently been shown, in principle, to admit unusual anyonic order, associated with Bloch Hopfions localized in momentum space. Here we show that bounding the integrated quantum metric along one primitive Brillouin-zone cycle may refine this topological order to $|C|$ distinct braiding observables, cyclically permuted by lattice translations, for Chern numbers $|C| > 1$. The cyclic structure entails mildly non-abelian braiding phases and otherwise matches the spectral flow exhibited by the FCI's hybrid Wannier states, with the metric bound equivalently a bound on the states' real-space spread. We give a classification of quantum gates in principle implementable on this topological order; among them we find the non-Clifford T-gate and the non-Clifford entangling CCZ-gate. This points to novel pathways to fault-tolerant quantum processes within the known orbital structure of FCIs, potentially informing experimental searches towards hardware for future topological quantum computers.
item.dc:creator: Hisham Sati, Urs Schreiber

item.title: Signatures of slow particle transport in the interacting Aubry-Andr\'e chain
item.description: arXiv:2610.25557v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Slow delocalization in strongly disordered many-body quantum chains can originate from two distinct mechanisms: rare resonances and avalanches, rooted in the energy statistics, or an energy-independent combinatorial path-entropy obstruction in operator space. Quasiperiodic potentials eliminate rare regions with similar potentials that are thought to be responsible for avalanche instabilities and modify the statistics of resonances, thus allowing us to delineate the two mechanisms. To do so, we numerically study the entanglement entropy $S(t)$, number entropy $S_N(t)$, and Hartley number entropy $S_H(t)$ following a quantum quench in the interacting Aubry-Andr\'e chain with disorder strength $D$. We find $S(t)\sim\mu\ln t$, $S_N(t)\sim\nu\ln\ln t$ with growth rates $\mu\sim\nu\sim D^{-\gamma}$ and $\gamma\approx 3$, the same behavior that was previously found in the case of quenched disorder. Furthermore, the saturation values $S_H(t\to\infty)$ continue to grow with system size $L$ as $\ln L$, a growth that persists for $D\gtrsim 8$ where MBL was argued to be stable. The similarity of the quasi-periodic and quenched disorder cases points to a common origin of the slow particle transport that does not rely on rare-region avalanches and persists despite strongly modified resonance statistics.
item.dc:creator: S. Sharifan, M. Kiefer-Emmanouilidis, J. Sirker

item.title: Engineering topological phenomena via field-driven Weyl motion
item.description: arXiv:2610.25609v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We illustrate the field-driven anomalous Hall engineering via the momentum-space motion of Weyl nodes using pyrochlore iridates under a [111] magnetic field as an example. We model the system with a well-established microscopic Hamiltonian and the field effect with the spin rotation from the all-in-all-out to the ferromagnetic state. Tracking the position of Weyl nodes during the spin rotation, we demonstrate macroscopic anomalous Hall conductivity variations are fundamentally driven by Weyl node motions by comparing the full multi-band Kubo formula with the geometric Weyl node separation. The discrepancy occurs only near a critical spin rotation angle, where several Weyl nodes come into close proximity. We reveal that the evolution of anomalous Hall conductivity under the magnetic field agrees with reported experiments in an order-of-magnitude and non-monotonicity. These results elucidate the field-driven dynamics of momentum-space monopoles and provide a framework for understanding transport in strongly correlated topological materials.
item.dc:creator: Jeonghoon Shin, Taekoo Oh

item.title: Spatiotemporal Imaging of Thermally Driven Metal-Insulator Phase Domain Propagation in VO2
item.description: arXiv:2610.26367v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Achieving a detailed picture of the nature and dynamics of phase boundaries remains a major challenge, particularly solid-solid transitions central to phase-change materials. Here, we use stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy and finite-element simulations to study the nonlinear thermally driven motion of the mesoscale insulator-metal phase boundary in VO2 thin films. We visualize the lateral spatiotemporal evolution of a diffraction-limited photoinduced metallic phase domain, resolving its outward propagation, contraction, and ultimate disappearance. The phase boundary dynamics are governed by heat flow, which can be controlled by excitation fluence, film thickness, and substrate thermal conductivity. Parameter-free agreement between the data and nonlinear thermal transport simulations identify the phase boundary transport as locally diffusive under this regime. We quantify how the latent heat acts as a thermal inertia, suppressing transport and prolonging the phase coexistence. Paradoxically, despite being driven by the underlying thermal gradient locally described by Fourier's law, the mesoscale phase front propagates faster than expected from thermal diffusion. This phenomenon arises from the distinction between temperature-field evolution and phase-boundary isotherm motion. These results establish a link between heat dissipation and mesoscale phase-front motion, providing a framework for controlling phase-transition kinetics relevant to photonics applications of VO2. We anticipate that this approach generalizes to a broad class of first- and second-order transitions.

item.title: Exploring ground state phase diagrams of Rydberg atom arrays with finite projected entangled-pair states
item.description: arXiv:2610.26520v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rydberg atom arrays (RAA) have been advocated as a promising avenue for the quantum simulation of different exotic quantum states. Numerical predictions for the ground state properties of this experimental platform can, however, be challenging in two-dimensional setups. In particular, faithfully treating long-range interactions is often crucial for distinguishing the fate of competing phases, but it usually comes at considerable cost. Projected entangled-pair states (PEPS), optimized via a sampling-based approach, have been shown to deal with such terms on the same ground as shorter-range ones. In this work, we employ these tools to investigate debated physical questions in different frustrated geometries of RAA, from the emergence of spin-glass physics on the Kagom\'e lattice to topological order beyond the PXP model on the Ruby lattice. By that, we contribute to establishing PEPS as well-suited tools for creating digital twins of RAA experiments.
item.dc:creator: Konrad Schr\"oder, Erik Lennart Weerda, Matteo Rizzi

item.title: Nucleation-type criticality with infinite number of free-energy minima beyond mean-field theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.26638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the phase diagram of a three-dimensional Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinski--Moriya interaction under the presence of Potts-like anisotropy. The phase transition between the winding phase and the ferromagnetically ordered phase exhibits a critical phase transition with anomalous features such as critical exponents consistent with that of a first-order transition while maintaining continuity of physical quantities. Furthermore, at the critical point, we see a growing number of free energy local minima, supporting the picture of infinitely many discontinuous transitions forming criticality. Our numerical result unify de Gennes' theory of nucleation-type transitions and Dzyaloshinskii's calculation of chiral magnets by demonstrating that such anomalous criticality can be realized in microscopic models beyond mean-field.
item.dc:creator: Jun Takahashi, Yoshihiko Nishikawa

item.title: Coherence and pairing enhancement in a trilayer cuprate with layer-selective charge order
item.description: arXiv:2506.01448v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Trilayer cuprates hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures ($T_{\text{c}}$), yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES), we uncover a striking interplay between charge order, superconducting gap magnitude, and quasiparticle coherence in Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{10+\delta}$ (Bi2223). We present ARPES-based evidence of charge order on the inner CuO$_2$ plane -- as confirmed via resonant x-ray scattering (RXS) -- and show that the same inner plane hosts a large superconducting gap matching its doping, firmly establishing it as underdoped. Despite its underdoped nature, the inner plane also exhibits an exceptional degree of quasiparticle coherence; suppressing charge-order fluctuations further enhances this, making it comparable to that of the overdoped outer planes at elevated electronic temperatures. At the same time, on the overdoped outer planes we find larger superconducting gaps than what is seen on comparably doped single and bilayer cuprates, indicating an unexpected and simultaneous enhancement of both coherence and pairing interactions in Bi2223. These findings, supported by complementary single- and three-layer Hubbard model calculations, reveal a unique interlayer mechanism in which both pairing strength and phase coherence are optimized when interfacing planes with distinct hole concentrations, providing new microscopic insight into the record $T_{\text{c}}$ of Bi2223.

item.title: Linear Ensemble-Constrained Quantum Monte Carlo: From Dilute Fermi Gas to Flat-Band Ferromagnetism
item.description: arXiv:2601.08552v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a finite-temperature canonical-ensemble determinant quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that enforces an exact fermion number and enables numerically stable simulations of correlated lattice fermions. We propose a stabilized QR update that reduces the computational complexity from standard cubic scaling $O(\beta N^3)$ to linear scaling $O(\beta N N_e^2)$ with respect to the system size $N$, where $N_e$ is the particle number. This yields a dramatic speedup in dilute regimes ($N_e \ll N$), opening unbiased access to large-scale simulations of strongly correlated low-density phases. We validate the method on the dilute Fermi gas with onsite Hubbard interactions, observing the suppression of the fermion sign problem in the dilute limit. Furthermore, we apply this approach to a one-dimensional flat-band system, where the canonical ensemble allows for precise control over filling. We reveal a ferromagnetic instability at low temperatures in the half-filling regime. Our linear-scaling approach provides a powerful tool for investigating emergent phenomena in dilute quantum matter.
item.dc:creator: Tu Hong, Kun Chen, Xiao Yan Xu

item.title: Dualities and Topological Classification of the $S=1$ Pyrochlore Spin Ice
item.description: arXiv:2603.03852v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive dual descriptions of the trivial paramagnetic, $\mathbb{Z}_2$-deconfined, and $\mathbb{Z}_2$-confined U(1) Coulomb phases of the $S=1$ pyrochlore spin ice. In the monopole-free limit, the system can be effectively mapped onto 3D $XY$ and Ising loop-gas models depending on the spin anisotropy, which provides theoretical estimates for the phase boundaries, while a macroscopic flux vector classifies the topological sectors via geometric parity rules. Thermal unit monopoles permit endpoints of both directed spin loops and unoriented vacancy loops. The resulting relevant symmetry-breaking fields in the dual $XY$ and Ising descriptions predict rounded crossovers near the monopole-free critical points. Monte Carlo simulations support this monopole-induced rounding.
item.dc:creator: Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, Haruki Watanabe

item.title: Topological Phase Transitions and Their Thermodynamic Fate in Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
item.description: arXiv:2604.04346v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a self-contained theoretical framework that classifies the topological phases and critical phenomena of classical pyrochlore magnets with arbitrary spin $S$, subject to competing exchange and single-ion anisotropies. We work first in the monopole-free (ice-rule) limit. In the small-$w$ regime, where the single-ion term favors low spin amplitudes, dualities reveal a dichotomy: Integer spins exhibit a continuous 3D $XY$ deconfinement transition, whereas half-integer spins remain in a $U(1)$ Coulomb liquid without any transition. In the large-$w$ regime, where $|S^z| = S$, the macroscopic flux is quantized to multiples of $2S$. Mapping the defect structure to loop gases, we prove that the ice rule is compatible with the modular $\mathbb{Z}_{2S}$ flux conservation at the vertex level if and only if $S \le 3/2$. For $S=3/2$, this maps the system to the three-state Potts model, whose symmetry-allowed cubic invariant drives a first-order transition. For $S \ge 2$, no discrete clock mapping exists; a decomposition of the partition function shows that the only processes sensitive to the discrete $\mathbb{Z}_{2S}$ structure carry exponentially small weight and correspond to irrelevant operators at the 3D $XY$ fixed point, so the deconfinement transition is of the 3D $XY$ type. Finally, incorporating thermal monopoles, we show that they act as a symmetry-breaking effective magnetic field that severs defect strings. Consequently, the continuous transitions are rounded into crossovers, whereas the first-order $S=3/2$ transition is predicted to survive at finite temperatures, terminating at a critical end point. Classical Monte Carlo simulations for $S$ up to $7/2$ corroborate the predicted crossovers at the accessible temperatures, which lie above the estimated critical end point, so the survival of the $S=3/2$ first-order transition remains to be tested directly.
item.dc:creator: Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, Haruki Watanabe

item.title: First-Principles Effective Mass in the Three-Dimensional Uniform Electron Gas
item.description: arXiv:2605.02294v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The quasiparticle effective mass $m^*$ of the three-dimensional uniform electron gas (UEG) is a fundamental Fermi-liquid parameter whose value and density dependence have remained controversial for decades. Using renormalized perturbation theory with explicit counterterms, we determine $m^*$ in the metallic regime ($r_s \le 6$) from first principles by two complementary routes -- the self-energy and the forward-scattering four-point vertex via the $p$-wave spin-symmetric Landau parameter $F_1^s$ -- that agree within uncertainties at each density through sixth renormalized order. The resulting $m^*/m$ remains close to unity throughout the metallic regime, with a shallow non-monotonic density dependence -- a minimum near $r_s\approx 1$ followed by a gentle upturn -- reflecting the interplay of exchange and dynamical screening in the self-energy, and disfavoring strong monotonic suppression. This finding supports a physical picture for the metallic UEG in which dominant charge correlations are concentrated in nearly forward scattering and generate only a weak $F_1^s$ component.
item.dc:creator: Pengcheng Hou, Daniel Cerkoney, Zhiyi Li, Tao Wang, Xiansheng Cai, Lei Wang, Gabriel Kotliar, Youjin Deng, Kun Chen

item.title: Algebraic Structure of Finite-Size Bethe Solutions in the Heisenberg Chain
item.description: arXiv:2605.05589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The spin-$1/2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain is the canonical example of an integrable quantum many-body model. Despite its exact solvability, explicit finite-size solutions are typically only accessible via numerical evaluation of the Bethe ansatz equations. Here, we analyse the algebraic structure of the exact, symbolic ground states for chains up to twelve sites using the Bethe ansatz. We find that the algebraic degree of the ground state magnon phases and Bethe roots scale with respect to system size at a different rate to the ground-state energy and wavefunction coefficients. The ground-state Bethe roots and energy are found to become Galois unsolvable for ten or more sites, thus demonstrating the lack of a symbolic analytical solution in a quantum integrable model due to algebraic complexity.
item.dc:creator: Oliver R. Bellwood, William J. Munro

item.title: Opto-criticality in Drude metals near the plasma frequency
item.description: arXiv:2605.08107v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Within a simple unified framework of classical electrodynamics that incorporates background bound charges and currents, we have analytically determined the attenuation constant, phase constant, and reflectivity of Drude metals across the full frequency spectrum ($0 < \omega < \infty$).Our result for reflectivity agrees well with existing experimental data for both plasmas and seawater. Notably, for highly conductive Drude metals ($\omega_p \tau \gg 1$), the attenuation constant simplifies to $k_- \simeq \sqrt{\frac{\mu \epsilon}{2}} \sqrt{\omega_p^2 - \omega^2 + \vert{}\omega_p^2 - \omega^2\vert{}}$ across a broad high-frequency range spanning the plasma frequency $\omega_p$. The branch-point singularity at $\omega=\omega_p$ in this relation reveals opto-critical behavior near $\omega=\omega_p$ in properties such as the attenuation constant, group velocity, and complex dielectric constant, for which we have determined the corresponding opto-critical exponents. Furthermore, we have incorporated quantum corrections into these optical properties via the Drude-Sommerfeld model with Thomas-Fermi screening.
item.dc:creator: Bikram Keshari Behera, Rhitabrata Bhattacharyya, Shyamal Biswas

item.title: Theory of two-dimensional Wigner crystals with defects: Interactions, melting transitions and collective modes
item.description: arXiv:2607.18477v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The physics of Wigner solids is characterized by an interplay of elasticity and long-range electrostatics, endowing crystal defects with properties distinct from those in charge-neutral crystals. Recent experiments observing lattice melting and Wigner-crystal-adjacent phases in two dimensions necessitate an examination of how defects affect the long-wavelength properties of such solids. Here, we use duality techniques to construct a comprehensive framework for studying the contribution of vacancies and interstitials, dislocations, and disclinations to the effective action of two-dimensional charged crystals. This allows for a systematic investigation of the interaction energies for the different combinations of defect pairs. We further study melting transitions due to defect proliferation, assessing and justifying some of the assumptions present in the literature. In the metallic Wigner crystal phase, characterized by a finite ground state density of vacancies, we find phonons with a dispersion relation that varies in an unusual way with the vacancy density. Consequently, we discuss how thermodynamic properties of such a vacancy Fermi liquid can be probed in measurements of the melting temperature and speed of sound. The field theory developed here can serve as a starting point in the study of anomalous Hall crystals and charge density waves with defects.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Matus, Tobias Holder

item.title: Resolving Spectral Gaps of the Frustrated Spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ Chain via Dual Spin-Sector Variational Quantum Eigensolver
item.description: arXiv:2610.10454v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Finding excited states and resolving spectral gaps in frustrated quantum spin systems using Variational Quantum Eigensolvers is complicated by state-ordering inversions. In the frustrated spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg chain, standard single-sector variational quantum deflation collapses onto intermediate triplet excitation, preventing the isolation of excited singlets and the singlet-singlet gap. To resolve these gaps, a Dual Spin-Sector Variational Quantum Eigensolver framework is introduced for near-term quantum architectures. By partitioning the search across magnetization sectors $S^z=0$ and $S^z=1$, the lowest triplet is resolved as an unconstrained ground state in $S^z=1$ with zero deflation penalty. Leveraging exact global spin-rotation symmetry, this state is mapped analytically into $S^z=0$ without ancilla overhead, unlocking dual deflation via shallow compute-uncompute circuits. Tracking both singlet-triplet and singlet-singlet gaps across coupling ratios $J_2/J_1$ from $0$ to $1$ for chains up to $16$ qubits faithfully captures all critical phenomena: the continuous Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition, exact Majumdar-Ghosh dimer degeneracy, level-ordering inversion in the gapless liquid phase, and incommensurate spiral excitations. Circuit depth scaling up to twenty layers provides an overparameterization mechanism overcoming classical local minima in strongly frustrated regimes, reducing relative energy errors below $1\%$ and elevating state fidelities above $97\%$ on $16$ qubits. Projective measurement sampling demonstrates resilience against shot noise, providing a practical blueprint for exploring frustrated quantum magnetism on near-term quantum devices.
item.dc:creator: Sk Saniur Rahaman

item.title: Spin Chain with Continuous Exponential Symmetry: Topological Phase and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.10682v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study symmetric gapped ground states of one-dimensional spin $S$ chains with a continuous exponential symmetry $U(1)\rtimes\mathbb Z_2$ with integer base $q$, where the U(1) charge has a modulated unit of charge $q^{L-j}$ decaying exponentially with site $j$. The simplest model is a quantum breakdown model that can be viewed as a $q$-deformation of the XXZ Haldane spin chain. We show that the topology of their symmetric ground states crucially depends on $S$ and $q$. For integer $S$, odd $q$ allows a nontrivial $\mathbb Z_2$ Haldane-type symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase with protected edge modes, while even $q$ allows no nontrivial SPT phase. For half-odd integer $S$, odd $q$ prohibits any unique symmetric gapped ground state due to a Lieb-Schultz-Mattis obstruction, whereas even $q$ enforces a novel symmetric gapped phase which we name as the ``half-SPT" phase. Unconventionally, the half-SPT phase only has a symmetry protected edge mode on one edge, and has half of the string orders of an SPT phase. Our results uncover a new type of symmetry-protected gapped phases beyond existing classification schemes.
item.dc:creator: Biao Lian, Zhen Bi

item.title: Symmetry-Adapted Eigensolver from Real-Space Sampling of Tensor-Network-Bridged Quantum Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2510.19219v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a symmetry-adapted eigensolver for strongly correlated systems that separates where the wave function is \emph{sampled} from where it is \emph{defined}. The lattice is divided into equal blocks: parallel quantum circuits absorb the entanglement within each block, while a matrix product state (MPS) backbone bridges the blocks and restores global correlations. The resulting real-space amplitude $\phi(a_{\rm real})$ acts only as a sample generator---configurations are drawn from $|\phi(a_{\rm real})|^2$ directly, block by block, without any Markov chain. The variational state itself is defined in a symmetry-adapted basis by two separate rules: the modulus of $\psi(a_{\rm symm})$ is the square root of the total weight accumulated over the entire equivalence class, $\widetilde{p}(a_{\rm symm})=\sum_{a_{\rm real}\in\{g a_{\rm repr}\}}|\phi(a_{\rm real})|^2$, whereas its phase is inherited from the single representative amplitude $\phi(a_{\rm repr})$. The modulus rule is what makes the scheme both exact and cheap: the distribution$\widetilde{p}(a_{\rm symm})$ sampled in the symmetric basis is exactly the one induced by the mapping from the real-space distribution $p(a_{\rm real})$, so every generated configuration is an unbiased sample of $|\psi(a_{\rm symm})|^2$; the phase rule then fixes the only freedom that remains. Because amplitudes within a class are combined in probability rather than summed with symmetry characters, $\psi$ is \emph{not} a group projection of the circuit-MPS state; the class-wide aggregation instead supplies long-range, symmetry-enforced entanglement that the MPS never has to carry itself.

item.title: A chemical avenue to manipulate field-reentrant superconducting rivalries in infinite layer nickelates
item.description: arXiv:2511.22026v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently, preliminary magnetic field-reentrant superconductivity manifested in high-temperature (Tc) Eu-doped infinite-layer (IL) nickelates, beyond analogous discoveries exclusively in low-Tc systems. This evokes intriguing fundamental issues about potential quantum-phase boundary and criticality between unconventional superconductivity and field-reentrant-one, which are inexplicable owing to formidable challenges in growing IL-nickelates towards later-series rare-earths. Herein, we open up chemical avenues to enable effective growth of (RE1-yRE'y)1-xEuxNiO2 (RE/RE': Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd, Dy), giving rise to discoveries of RE-4f-related quantum competition between high-Tc and reentrant superconductivity. Robust magnetic-field-reentrant superconductivity with uniaxial anisotropy is observed at superconducting-dome boundaries, stemming from Eu2+-4f7 associated competition between magnetic-fluctuation promoted pairing and exchange-field interactions. Their quantum-criticality is further modulable via RE(RE')-magnetism, which either reinforces reentrancy or elevates Tc (40.1 K) with more robust critical-current-density (~266 kA/cm2 at 2 K) beyond Sr-/Ca-doped counterparts. Our synthetic route enables the establishment of an ideal platform via IL-nickelates for studying 4f-related unconventional superconductivity and quantum-criticality.

item.title: Interaction and disorder effects on Cooper instability in two-dimensional fractional Dirac semimetals
item.description: arXiv:2602.22772v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Employing a renormalization group analysis that allows for an unbiased treatment of competing physical ingredients, we systematically trace how the interplay between Cooper pairing and disorder scatterings governs the emergence or suppression of Cooper instability in the low-energy regime of fractional Dirac semimetals.In the clean limit, we find that the emergence of Cooper instability requires surpassing a finite interaction threshold $|\lambda_c|$, and depends sensitively on both the fractional exponent $\alpha$ and the transfer momentum $\mathbf{Q}=(Q,\phi)$. Specifically, bigger values of $\alpha$ enhance the tendency toward BCS instability. For $\alpha\in(0.001,0.61)$, the $(Q,\phi)$ parameter space separates into two distinct regions: Zone-\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral1}, where Cooper instability is suppressed, and Zone-\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral2}, where it is allowed. In the presence of disorders, we demonstrate that they can either promote or suppress Cooper instability. Disorder of type $\Delta_1$ or $\Delta_2$ enhances superconductivity by reducing the critical interaction threshold $|\lambda_c|$ and expanding the superconducting phase space (Zone-\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral2}). In sharp contrast, either $\Delta_0$ or $\Delta_3$ suppresses Cooper pairing by increasing $|\lambda_c|$ and shrinking the available phase space (Zone-\uppercase\expandafter{\romannumeral1}). Although Cooper instability can be enhanced when promotive disorders ($\Delta_1$, $\Delta_2$) coexist with a single suppressive disorder ($\Delta_0$ or $\Delta_3$), the suppressive influence of $\Delta_{0,3}$ generally dominates the promotive effects of $\Delta_{1,2}$ in the presence of all sorts of disorders. These results would be helpful for further studies of fractional Dirac semimetals and alike materials.

item.title: Quantum matter is weakly entangled at low energies
item.description: arXiv:2604.14143v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct upper bounds on entanglement entropies of many-body quantum states that have fixed energy expectation values with respect to local Hamiltonians. Our focus is on entanglement entropies of subsystems that make up approximately half of the full system. The upper bound on the von Neumann entanglement entropy is half the sum of the thermal entropies of two fictitious systems at the same temperature as one another, with an additional area-law contribution in some systems. The effective temperature is chosen such that the sum of the thermal energies of the two fictitious systems matches the constraint on the energy of the state in the original problem; at subextensive energies, this temperature decreases with increasing system size. Our upper bounds on R\'{e}nyi entanglement entropies take an analogous form. These inequalities show that, in systems that are frustration-free (FF) and whose zero-temperature subsystem thermal entropies scale with surface areas (rather than subsystem volumes), ground states are area-law entangled. For physical models of quantum matter, which have well-defined specific heat capacities (and are not necessarily FF), our bounds provide a way to convert this thermodynamic data into constraints on pure-state entanglement at both subextensive and extensive energies. We also show that our general upper bounds on half-system entanglement entropies are optimal, up to subleading corrections, in systems with reflection symmetry and above a subextensive energy threshold. A key application of our results is to constrain the entanglement of quantum states relevant to simulations of zero-temperature response functions, which have energies of order unity. We prove that, in wide varieties of FF systems in two dimensions and higher, the contributions of excitations to von Neumann entanglement entropy are subleading compared with the contribution from the ground state.

item.title: Learning Effective Bulk Fields from Fermionic Spectra: Application to an Extended Power-Law Liquid Model for Cuprate Strange Metals
item.description: arXiv:2607.02861v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a Neural-ODE framework to infer effective bulk metric functions and the charge-weighted gauge potential from boundary fermionic spectra within a static, planar black-hole ansatz. Controlled benchmarks recover the known bulk profiles of the Einstein--Maxwell and Gubser--Rocha models. We then use normalized interaction self-energy targets generated from an extended power-law liquid model with parameters calibrated by angle-resolved photoemission measurements to test the proposed geometric explanation of cuprate strange-metal spectra in a semi-holographic setting. For this application, we use a massless probe in backgrounds with conformal-to-$\mathrm{AdS}_2\times\mathbb{R}^2$ asymptotics and derive a spectral extraction formula from the conserved radial Dirac flux. We identify coordinate/Weyl redundancy and a degeneracy in the scaled Hawking temperature of the normalized inverse problem. The conformal factor remains undetermined, so bulk entropy and the associated contribution to electronic specific heat require independent input. Low-temperature targets are fitted accurately across the studied doping range. In the high-temperature test, however, the present ansatz and optimization search have not yielded a refined geometry that accurately reproduces the thermal spectral shape while preserving frequency symmetry. These results may guide the further development of semi-holographic models for cuprates, and the framework may also find applications in other strongly correlated electron systems.

item.title: Nonlinear quantum multi-spin dynamics without entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2610.05521v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a distinct route for extending classical atomistic spin dynamics into the quantum regime for arbitrary spin $s$, based on a variational product-state \textit{ansatz} that includes both pure and mixed local states. By construction, intersite entanglement -- expected to remain negligible even on very short time scales in many real materials -- is excluded, while local quantum effects are retained through the nonclassical structure of $s\geq 1$ density operators. Nonlinear dynamics arise from both the mean-field interdependence of the local states and the state-dependent dissipative terms. The framework recovers classical spin dynamics for $s=\frac{1}{2}$ while allowing genuinely quantum local dynamics for higher spins. It clarifies the variational and geometric origin of the inequivalence between quantum Landau-Lifshitz and Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics, provides a criterion for their equivalence under a common time rescaling, establishes connections with the classical theory through two qualitatively distinct limits ($s\to\infty$ and a large number of quantum spins $N$), and allows realistic $\mathcal{O}(N)$ simulations of quantum spin dynamics in materials.

item.title: Characterizing Fermionic Non-Gaussianity in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model via Replica Twist Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2610.10123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding the non-equilibrium dynamics of quantum many-body systems plays a central role in modern many-body physics. Intriguing insights emerge from investigating how quantum resources, which are essential for achieving unambiguous quantumness, are generated and spread under chaotic quantum dynamics. In fermionic systems, non-Gaussianity constitutes an important resource beyond entanglement, characterizing the deviation of generic quantum states from free-fermion states. In this Letter, we propose using the \textit{replica twist entropy}, defined through the expectation value of a replica rotation operator with a tunable angle $\alpha$, as a natural probe of non-Gaussianity in pure fermionic states. After deriving its behavior for typical many-body states, we establish a general framework for analyzing the replica twist entropy in solvable Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models in the large-$N$ limit. Applying this framework to the dynamics of the thermofield double state, we uncover a novel dynamical phase diagram in the parameter space of $\alpha$ and evolution time $t$, exhibiting spontaneous $Z_2$ symmetry breaking at $\alpha=\pi/4$ and universal cusps as a function of $\alpha$ in the long-time regime. Our results pave the way for studying non-Gaussianity in strongly correlated fermionic systems and reveal a new class of dynamical transitions probed by non-Gaussianity.

item.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions with nontrivial electronic bands
item.description: arXiv:2610.13246v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. Despite the theoretical and experimental significance of these phenomena, a microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions that takes into account the full composite nature of these quasiparticles in systems with an arbitrary single-particle Hamiltonian is lacking. Here, we present a general theory of exciton-exciton interactions that builds upon our previous publication [Physical Review B 113, 155440 (2026)], which applied only to conventional semiconductors with weak band hybridization. By contrast, the theory presented here is valid in virtually any crystalline semiconducting system and can be applied to the study of biexciton formation and correlated excitonic phases in systems where band topology, quantum geometry, and moir\'e effects play a significant role. In addition to the analytical theory, we also present results in simple systems with flat bands with a nontrivial quantum metric and show that the biexcitonic spectrum differs strongly from that in the case without quantum geometry. Our theory paves the way for accurate quantitative calculations of biexciton spectra and excitonic many-body phases in modern condensed-matter systems.
